newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK output prices to stay subdued in Sept.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK output prices to stay subdued in Sept.

text.p: Lower raw material and unit wage costs should keep British factory gate prices subdued in September and City analysts said on Friday they expect only a neglible rise in producers' output prices.
The figures are due on Monday at 0830 GMT and the Reuters consensus forecast suggests a 0.1 percent rise in output prices on the month compared with unchanged prices in August.
The year-on-year rate is expected to ease to up 1.8 percent from 2.0 percent in August.

"The most significant factor is that growth in unit wage costs has slowed since the beginning of the year," said Dharshini David, analyst at HSBC Markets. "And raw material costs, apart from oil, remain low."
Recent survey evidence also strengthens the case for only a marginal rise in prices.
"The CBI's price balance remains historically low at zero percent suggesting that output price pressures will continued to be light," said Ciaran Barr, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Output prices have declined steadily this year, feeling the effects of lower commodity prices across the board.
But the recent sharp rise in oil prices means the outlook for input prices is not so favourable.
The consensus forecast suggests a 0.5 percent rise in input prices although the year-on-year rates could fall further, to 2.4 percent from 2.2 percent in August.
"The rise is largely due to the surge in oil prices, up by an average of 12 percent in September on August, caused by renewed anxiety over the situation in the Gulf in early September," said David.
This will more than offset lower prices in foods and metals.
"The rise in oil prices will also offset the benefits of a stronger pound," said Barr. He forecasts a 0.8 percent rise in input price in the month.
But the oil price move may be a one off.
"We view the oil price rise as transitory and so further falls in the month-on-month rate are feasible, especially if the price of Brent crude falls back," said David.
And if sterling makes further gains, especially against the dollar, input inflation stands to diminish even further.
Sterling has appreciated by almost 4.0 percent on a trade- weighted basis in the last two months.
